newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB files complaint against CN, CP Rail service.
newsitem.headline: CWB files complaint against CN, CP Rail service.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board said on Monday it filed a complaint with the federal Canadian Transportation Agency claiming substandard service from CP Rail System and Canadian National Railway Co on grain shipping.

The CWB exports all of Western Canada's wheat and barley, with annual sales of more than C$5 billion. But rail shipping delays have cost the CWB more than C$20 million in demurrage charges since January, the CWB said on April 1.

"The CWB charges that CN and CP have failed to provide adequate transpoortation services for grain movement from the Prairie provinces to eastern and western ports and to U.S. destinations," the wheat board said in a statement.
"Poor railway performance this crop year has seriously affected the CWB sales program, pool return revenue, farmer delivery opportunities and demurrage costs," it said.
The Canadian Transportation Agency, the regulatory body for Canadian railroads, must investigate the complaint and "determine proper recourse" with 120 days, the CWB said.
